title: Dispatch jobs to a worker pool
summary: Schedule jobs across a fixed set of workers, giving each job to the next idle worker and queueing the rest, like a cluster or thread pool.
prompt:
Finish `WorkerPool`. It is built with an array of workers; each worker is an async function `(job) => Promise<result>` that handles one job at a time.

- `run(job)` returns a promise of the result. If a worker is idle, give the job to the idle worker that comes next in round-robin order after the last one used. Otherwise queue the job (first in, first out) until a worker becomes free.
- A failing job rejects only its own promise; the worker becomes idle again.
- `stats()` returns `{ busy, queued }`.
hints: Track `busy: boolean[]` and a `cursor` for round-robin.
To pick a worker, check indexes `cursor, cursor + 1, ...` modulo the length and take the first idle one.
When a job settles (use `finally`), mark the worker idle and start the next queued job.
